newsitem.title: CHILE: Quebrada Blanca copper strike talks unsuccessful.
newsitem.headline: Quebrada Blanca copper strike talks unsuccessful.

text.p: A new round of strike talks at Chile's Quebrada Blanca copper mine ended without agreement on Sunday as workers held out for special compensation for working at high altitude, union president Nelson Fuentes said.

"Unfortunately there is no positive result to report. We continue on indefinite strike," Fuentes told Reuters by telephone from the northern city of Iquique, where the union leadership has been meeting with Quebrada Blanca general manager Jim Drake.
Workers at the 75,000-tonne-a-year mine, owned by Canada's Cominco Ltd, went on strike last Wednesday after weeks of negotiations failed to yield a new wage contract.
Management could not be reached for comment. The company has given no public comment on the strike's effects on production and stockpiles.

Fuentes said the main issue of contention was miners' demands for special compensation for working at high altitude. One of the highest copper mines in the world, Quebrada Blanca lies at 4,200 meters above sea level on an arid plateau near the Bolivian border.

Workers currently receive a differential to compensate for the extreme isolation of the mine, which is hours away from the nearest town, but want an additional payment for the health effects of working at high altitude, said Fuentes. The union was seeking about 30,000 pesos ($73 U.S.) a month more per worker than the firm was offering so far, he said.
Talks were continuing in a cordial atmosphere and the union were still optimistic about reaching a solution in the next few days, he said. ((--Roger Atwood, Santiago newsroom +56-2-699-5595 x211))
